title: Trace metadata canonicalization + Privacy Gatekeeper for levelled retention
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Goal: Introduce a lightweight Privacy Gatekeeper that canonicalizes trace metadata fields and enforces tiered retention levels before traces enter long-term storage. Rationale: current tracing pipeline allows diverse service-level trace attributes (user.email, user_id, session_token, query_text) that leak PII and make retention/returns inconsistent across tenants. This ticket builds an in-pipeline policy layer that standardizes field names, normalizes values, and applies a per-tenant retention level (Full, Pseudonymized, Schema-only) with auditable reveal controls.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Incoming traces pass through gatekeeper and fields are mapped to canonical keys (e.g., usr.email -> user.email_hashed, req.ip -> ip_prefix3) according to the configurable schema. 2) Retention level for tenant X can be set to Full, Pseudonymized, or Schema-only and persists across downstream sinks. 3) Any just-in-time reveal requests must be logged to the access ledger with actor, reason, and TTL. 4) End-to-end pipeline latency increase < 6ms p50 and < 12ms p95 for trace ingestion in canary region. 5) QA tests and e2e harness validate canonicalization rules for 12 example sensitive fields. 6) Console exposes per-tenant retention level and an audit view for recent reveals.
design_notes: Approach: implement gatekeeper as a sidecar filter in the collector tier (low-latency path) with a rule engine that applies transformations: normalization, hashing (HMAC-SHA256 with tenant-scoped salt), prefix-truncation for IPs, and token redaction. Store per-tenant policy in ConfigStore (existing SG config API) with cache TTL. Access reveals are gated by RBAC checks against internal authz service and require an ephemeral reveal token that expires and is recorded in audit stream. Trade-offs: doing canonicalization inline reduces complexity vs. an async sanitizer service but increases ingestion path coupling. To mitigate, gatekeeper is lightweight, pure-transform, and circuit-breaks to pass-through on config fetch failure.
implementation_plan: 1) Schema: define canonical key mapping and transformation types in confluence doc (link below). 2) Gatekeeper binary: implement Go filter using existing collector plugin API. 3) Config API: extend SG config to store tenant.policy.retention_level and canonical_rules. 4) RBAC hooks: call authz/verify with actor and scope for reveal operations. 5) Audit logging: emit reveal events to audit-sink with structured metadata. 6) Tests: unit tests for transform functions, integration tests in staging with synthetic PII traces, performance benchmark. 7) Rollout: start with internal tenants -> opt-in beta customers -> global default. 8) Dashboard: add controls and recent-reveals panel to Console. 9) Docs/Runbook: produce ops runbook for key rotation and recovery.
migration_notes: Backfill: On first-enforcement day, we will run an 'analyze-only' pass to report fields that would be modified without persisting changes. Use this to generate a remediation checklist for services producing non-canonical fields. For existing long-term storage, run a one-time scrub job for tenants that opt-in to pseudonymization. Preserve object IDs so downstream dashboards are not broken.
security_considerations: - Use KMS-backed tenant salts for HMAC hashing; do not store raw salts in plaintext. - Ensure reveal tokens are single-use and short TTL. - All reveal events go to immutable audit stream with tenant, actor, justification. - Security review required prior to canary. - Rate-limit reveal API to avoid exfiltration risk.
monitoring_and_slo: Track: gatekeeper_ingest_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99), transform_error_rate, config_fetch_failure_rate, reveal_success_rate, reveal_audit_sink_latency. SLOs: p95 ingest latency impact <= +8ms; transform_error_rate < 0.01%. Set alerts for config fetch errors and reveal failure rate spikes.
console_changes: - Add "Retention level" toggle in Tenant settings with explanatory tooltip. - Add "Recent reveals" table with filters by actor, tenant, and time. - Add a small heatmap showing percentage of traces per retention level per day.
testing_plan: Unit tests for each transform type. Integration tests using test-collector that can simulate high ingestion and random PII patterns. Canary will run in us-west-2 for 48h with traffic shaping: 5% of production traces. Run a chaos test where ConfigStore is unavailable to validate pass-through behaviour.
deployment_strategy: Blue/green for gatekeeper collector plugin with canary routing. Initial rollout to internal orgs only. Provide toggle to disable canonicalization per tenant in case of regressions. Run migration analyze-only window for 7 days prior to enforcement.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: mis-canonicalization breaks downstream tooling that depends on original keys. Mitigation: mapping layer kept in ConfigStore and a compatibility shim that emits both canonical and original keys behind an opt-in flag. Risk: KMS latency increasing reveal path time. Mitigation: cache ephemeral reveal tokens and pre-warm KMS on high-volume tenants.
